• Automated unit and integration tests, rerun on every change

Electronics and software:
• Watchdog and a defined safe state at startup, on fault and on power loss
• IEC #-# Annex H (Class B) if the software performs a safety function
• Coding rules (e.g. MISRA C), code review and static analysis before each release
• Automated unit and integration tests, rerun on every change
• Input validation, timeouts and automatic recovery of communications
• Non-volatile memory protected by CRC, writes limited to the memory's endurance
• Signed update with the possibility of rolling back to the previous version
• Sensors: filtering and debouncing, thresholds with hysteresis, measurement plausibility checks
Moving parts and service life:
• Service life specified in cycles, with a margin of at least # times the intended use
• Material pairs chosen against wear (plastic on metal, specified lubricant), not two identical plastics rubbing together
• Switches and buttons chosen for a known number of cycles (datasheet), with debouncing
• Adjustable friction or clamping, wear take-up provided
• No pinching or shearing of fingers by moving parts (IEC #-#, cl. #)

Industry best practices:
Structure and mechanics:
• Safety factor of at least # on structural parts (# for a plastic under long-term load: creep)
• Calculation or finite element simulation of loaded parts, including drop and impact cases
• Tolerance analysis (worst case or RSS) on every critical fit
• Fillets, no sharp corners or notches in a loaded area (stress concentration)
• Molded parts: uniform wall thickness, ribs, draft angles, material chosen with its datasheet
• Fasteners: specified torque, thread-locker or washer, metal inserts in plastic
• Stability: low center of gravity, tilt test on an inclined plane per the product standard
For any function:
• Purchased part: datasheet read in full, qualified supplier, second source identified
• Standard part (ISO, DIN) with its strength or precision class specified on the drawing
• Peer design review (PDR, CDR) with this DFMEA line in front of the reviewers
• Lessons learned: DFMEA and field feedback from a similar or previous product
• Proven solution or qualified off-the-shelf part rather than a new technology, unless there is a quantified reason
• Quantified, verifiable requirement in the functional specification (CdCF) (Goldmine) for this function, with its tolerance
